questions.q: What is required of every LWC HTML template file?
options: It must contain at least two sibling root elements
It must import `LightningElement` directly inside the HTML file
It must start and end with a single root `<template>` element
It must declare its own `js-meta.xml` configuration inline
questions.explain: Every LWC template file wraps all of its markup inside exactly one root `<template>` tag -- never raw HTML outside it, and never multiple sibling root elements.

questions.q: In `<lightning-button label="Save" onclick={handleSave}></lightning-button>`, why does `{handleSave}` have no parentheses?
options: It's passing a reference to the function so the framework can call it later, rather than calling it immediately during render
Parentheses are only used for getters, not event handlers
LWC templates don't support parentheses in any binding expression
Adding parentheses would make `handleSave` a reactive property
questions.explain: Writing `{handleSave}` without parentheses passes a reference to the method itself. If you called it with parentheses, the method would execute immediately while the template renders, instead of waiting for the click event.

questions.q: What is the current recommended directive set for conditional rendering in LWC, per this lesson?
options: if:true and if:false only, with no alternative
render:true and render:false
switch:case and switch:default
lwc:if, lwc:elseif, and lwc:else
questions.explain: lwc:if / lwc:elseif / lwc:else are the current recommended directives for conditional rendering. The older if:true / if:false directives still work and remain common in existing orgs, but they only support a true/false pair, not an elseif chain.

questions.q: Why does every element inside a `for:each` loop need a unique `key` attribute?
options: The `key` is purely cosmetic and has no effect on rendering
Without a `key`, the `for:each` directive throws a compile-time error and the component won't deploy
The framework uses the key to track which DOM nodes to reuse, move, or remove as the underlying array changes across re-renders
The `key` attribute sets the CSS class of each repeated element
questions.explain: The key gives the framework a stable way to tell list items apart across re-renders, so it can efficiently reuse, reorder, or remove the right DOM nodes instead of re-rendering the whole list from scratch.

questions.q: Why does `this.template.querySelector(...)` use `this.template` instead of the global `document`?
options: Because LWC renders into shadow DOM, and `this.template` scopes the search to the component's own shadow boundary rather than the whole page
Because `document.querySelector` is deprecated in all modern browsers
Because `this.template` is faster than `document` for every query, with no other difference
Because `document.querySelector` can only find `<div>` elements
questions.explain: LWC components render into shadow DOM, so `this.template.querySelector` deliberately only searches within the component's own shadow boundary -- it will not reach into a child component's internal markup, which is intentional encapsulation.
